## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limma, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, readr, ggplot2, writexl)
here::i_am("06_Composition/02_fibre_type/a_script/02_fibre_type.qmd")
```

## Read proteins and reference

FibeRtypeR (Van der Stede et al. 2026, doi:10.1113/JP290082) reads each biopsy as a mix of a pure
slow (type I) and a pure fast (type II) fibre profile. Its proteomics markers are the 77 slow and
68 fast proteins of its Table S1 (Shared and Proteome columns). The reference profile of each
marker is its mean log2 abundance in the 24 slow and 24 fast pre-training fibre pools of Moesgaard
et al. 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77275-9, PRIDE PXD056664), the data FibeRtypeR's proteomics
reference was built from; `references/fibertyper_reference.csv` holds both. The bulk input is the
limpa matrix rather than DIA-NN's MaxLFQ, because limpa's complete matrix measures more markers in
every sample.

```{r read}
stage <- here("06_Composition", "02_fibre_type")
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
reference <- read_csv(file.path(stage, "references", "fibertyper_reference.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE)
targets <- proteins$targets
stopifnot(identical(rownames(d$design), targets$sample_id))
count(reference, marker_type)
```

## Estimate the slow fraction

Markers are matched to the matrix by gene symbol, one row per symbol. Each sample is shifted so its
median over the markers equals the reference's, a project choice where the paper says only
"log2-normalized". For two fractions that are non-negative and sum to one, the least-squares fit
FibeRtypeR runs (DeconRNASeq, equivalently `limSolve::lsei()`) has a closed form: the projection of
the sample onto the line from the fast to the slow profile, clipped to [0, 1].

```{r deconvolve}
genes <- proteins$genes$Genes
rows <- which(genes %in% reference$gene & !duplicated(genes))
bulk <- proteins$E[rows, ]
profile <- reference[match(genes[rows], reference$gene), ]
bulk <- sweep(bulk, 2, apply(bulk, 2, median) - median(c(profile$slow_log2, profile$fast_log2)))
direction <- profile$slow_log2 - profile$fast_log2
slow <- colSums((bulk - profile$fast_log2) * direction) / sum(direction^2)
targets$slow <- pmin(pmax(slow, 0), 1)[targets$sample_id]
count(profile, marker_type)
summary(targets$slow)
```

## Checks without histology

No histology exists for these biopsies, so the level is unvalidated; the checks ask whether the
ranking behaves like fibre type: a person's two legs should agree, as should one leg's two biopsies,
most variation should sit between people, and women's muscle is usually slower than men's.

```{r checks}
wide <- targets |>
  select(participant, leg, timepoint, slow) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(leg, timepoint), values_from = slow)
checks <- tibble(
  check = c(
    "left vs right leg at T1 (r)", "same leg, T1 vs T2 (r)",
    "variance between participants (R2)", "women minus men (points)"
  ),
  value = c(
    cor(wide$L_T1, wide$R_T1, use = "complete.obs"),
    cor(c(wide$L_T1, wide$R_T1), c(wide$L_T2, wide$R_T2), use = "complete.obs"),
    summary(lm(slow ~ participant, targets))$r.squared,
    100 * (mean(targets$slow[targets$sex == "F"]) - mean(targets$slow[targets$sex == "M"]))
  )
)
mutate(checks, value = round(value, 2))
```

## Did training or arm shift fibre type?

The slow fraction goes through the stage 02 design (group, participant, blood index) and its five
contrasts as a single outcome row, so the test is the plain least-squares t, as for MPE in
`05_Mitochondria`. Estimates are in percentage points.

```{r contrasts}
fit <- contrasts.fit(lmFit(rbind(slow = 100 * targets$slow), d$design), d$contrasts)
contrasts <- tibble(
  contrast = colnames(d$contrasts), points = fit$coefficients[1, ],
  se = fit$stdev.unscaled[1, ] * fit$sigma, df = fit$df.residual
) |>
  mutate(
    p = 2 * pt(-abs(points / se), df),
    conf.low = points - qt(0.975, df) * se, conf.high = points + qt(0.975, df) * se
  )
group_summary <- targets |>
  summarise(mean = 100 * mean(slow), sd = 100 * sd(slow), n = n(), .by = c(treatment, timepoint))
group_summary
mutate(contrasts, across(where(is.double), function(x) signif(x, 3)))
```

## Figure

Each leg's slow fraction before and after training, one line per leg, by arm.

```{r figure}
figure <- targets |>
  mutate(leg_id = paste(participant, leg)) |>
  ggplot(aes(timepoint, 100 * slow, group = leg_id)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = treatment), size = 1.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(BFR = "#D55E00", HLRT = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Slow (type I) fibre fraction, %",
    title = "Fibre type before and after training") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9)
figure

pdf(file.path(stage, "b_reports", "02_fibre_type.pdf"), width = 8.27, height = 5)
print(figure)
invisible(dev.off())
```

## Save results

```{r write}
write_xlsx(
  list(
    slow_fraction = select(targets, sample_id, participant, leg, treatment, timepoint, sex, slow),
    contrasts = contrasts,
    group_summary = group_summary,
    checks = checks
  ),
  file.path(stage, "c_data", "02_fibre_type.xlsx")
)
```
